parameters.description: Only records of any of these types, such as Dataset, Software or Journal article. A main type such as Publication includes all of its kinds. Leave empty for every type.
parameters.name: resource_types

parameters.description: Only records whose files are open to anyone, under embargo, restricted to people the owner allows, or with no files at all. Leave empty for all.
parameters.name: access_status

parameters.description: Only records in this community: pick one, or type the name in its address (such as 'covid-19') or paste its link. Leave empty for all of Zenodo.
parameters.name: community

parameters.description: Only records by this person or organization: a name (every word must match, in any order) or an ORCID iD such as 0000-0002-2430-1612.
parameters.name: creator

parameters.description: Only records funded by this grant: its ID from 'Search grants' (such as 00k4n6c32::777541) or the funder's grant number.
parameters.name: grant

parameters.description: Only records with a file of this type, by its extension, such as pdf, csv or zip. Several can be separated by commas.
parameters.name: file_type

parameters.description: Only records published on this date or later.
parameters.name: published_after

parameters.description: Only records published on this date or earlier.
parameters.name: published_before

parameters.description: Return every version that matches, not just each record's newest version.
parameters.name: all_versions

parameters.description: The order of the results. Best match by default, which is newest first when there is no search text.
parameters.name: sort

parameters.description: How many records to return on a page, up to 25.
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: Which page of results to return, from 1. Zenodo pages through the first 10,000 matches only.
parameters.name: page

count.description: How many are on this page.

more_available.description: Whether a next page has more. Zenodo pages through the first 10,000 matches only.

access_status.description: Who can get its files: 'open' (anyone), 'embargoed' (anyone, after a date), 'restricted' (people the owner allows) or 'metadata-only' (no files).

slug.description: The community's name in its address, such as 'covid-19'. Every action that takes a community accepts it.

concept_doi.description: The DOI that always resolves to the newest version, the one to cite for 'any version'. Empty for a record with a DOI from elsewhere.

concept_id.description: The ID that stands for every version of the record. Giving it to an action means the newest version.

created.description: When it was put on Zenodo, as an ISO 8601 date and time.

creators.description: The people and organizations who made it, in order.

affiliation.description: Where they work, as the record gives it; several are separated by '; '.

orcid.description: Their ORCID iD, such as '0000-0002-2430-1612', when given.

description.description: Its description as plain text, a line per paragraph or list item.

doi_url.description: Its DOI as a link, such as 'https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.7559361'.

downloads.description: How many times this version's files were downloaded.

embargo_until.description: For an embargoed record, the date its files open, as 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

files.description: Its files, up to the first 100 (empty when they aren't public). 'List a record's files' gives every one.

download_url.description: The address that downloads the file.

name.description: The file's name, such as 'data.csv'. Names can contain folders, such as 'matplotlib/matplotlib-v3.11.2.zip'.

funder_name.description: The funder's name, such as 'European Commission'.

grant_id.description: The grant's ID, such as '00k4n6c32::777541'. 'Search records' takes it to find everything a grant funded.

grant_number.description: The funder's own number for the grant.

id.description: The record's ID, such as '7559361'. Each version of a record has its own.

is_latest.description: Whether it is the newest version.

license_id.description: Its licence's ID, such as 'cc-by-4.0' or 'mit'.

license_title.description: Its licence's name, such as 'Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International'.

license_url.description: A link to its licence's text.

publication_date.description: When it was published, as its creators give it: 'YYYY-MM-DD', or just a year or a month.

related_identifiers.description: Other works it is linked to, such as the paper it supplements or the code repository it was released from.

identifier.description: The other work's identifier, such as a DOI or a link.

relation.description: How the record relates to it, such as 'Is supplement to' or 'Cites'.

scheme.description: What kind of identifier it is, such as 'doi' or 'url'.

resource_type.description: What it is, as Zenodo's ID, such as 'dataset', 'software' or 'publication-article'.

resource_type_title.description: What it is, in words, such as 'Journal article'.

total_size.description: The size of all its files together, in bytes.

unique_downloads.description: How many visitors downloaded this version's files.

unique_views.description: How many visitors viewed this version's page.

updated.description: When it last changed, as an ISO 8601 date and time.

version.description: Its version as its creators name it, such as 'v3.11.2'.

version_index.description: Which version it is: 1 for the first, and so on.

views.description: How many times this version's page was viewed.

description: Search Zenodo, CERN's free open repository, for papers, datasets, software and other research outputs by type, community, creator, grant and publication date. Read a record's versions, files and statistics, see what is inside its zip files, cite it in APA or another style or export it as BibTeX or DataCite, and look up communities, licences, funders and grants. A trigger runs a workflow when a new record matches a search. No account or API key required.

zenodo_new_record_trigger.description: Runs when a record is published on Zenodo that matches search text, belongs to a community or is of a resource type, with its DOI, creators, description and licence. Records already there when the workflow is turned on don't run it.

parameters.description: Words a new record must match, in its title, description, creators or keywords, such as 'climate model'. Zenodo's search syntax works too. Give this, a community, a resource type, or any mix of them.
parameters.name: query

parameters.description: Only records in this community: the name in its address, such as 'covid-19', or its zenodo.org link. Leave blank for all of Zenodo.
parameters.name: community

parameters.description: Only records of this type, such as Dataset, Software or Journal article. Leave blank for every type.
parameters.name: resource_type
